 Oral Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant/KSRTC, under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
challenging the judgment and award dated 21.03.2018 passed in MVC No.1482/2016 by X Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, MACT, Bengaluru.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant.
Learned counsel for respondents remained absent.
The ranks of the parties are retained as per tribunal for the sake of convenience.
NC: 2025:KHC:34671 HC-KAR 3.
Brief facts of the case is that one Sundaresh, met with an accident on 24.07.2015.
The present appellants are mother and brother of the deceased filed claim application, claiming compensation of Rs.21,00,000/- before tribunal.

The tribunal considering the entire evidence on record, granted an amount of Rs.15,42,000/- and reduced 40% of the compensation awards towards contributory negligence and granted Rs.9,25,500/- with interest at the rate of 9% p.a., from the date of filing the petition till the date of realisation.
Aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is filed.

4. This appeal is preferred by the Insurance company and the main grievance is that the income should be taken as Rs.9,000/- per month as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Services Divisional Controller vs Smt. Sarojamma on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101964970/
2 Authority, but the tribunal erred in taking the notional income of Rs.10,000/- per month.

Therefore,
loss of dependency is calculated as 40% future prospects to be taken as per the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of NC: 2025:KHC:34671 HC-KAR National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in reported (2017)16 SCC 680 and since he was bachelor 50% to be deducted towards his personal expenses as per the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation Limited and Another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 1219.

Therefore, for Rs.9,000/-, 40% needs to be added and 50%
needs to be deducted.
Therefore, Rs.6,300 x 12 x 18 = Rs.13,60,800/- is loss of dependency.
5. The petitioner No.1 is the mother of the deceased and lost her son in her old age.
Therefore, she is entitled for filial consortium of Rs.40,000/-.

Apart from that, she is also entitled for Rs.30,000/-
under the conventional heads.
NC: 2025:KHC:34671 HC-KAR 6.

Thus in all, components awarded by this court are as below, Particulars Amount in Rs.
 Loss of dependency 13,60,800  Towards filial consortium 40,000  Conventional heads 30,000  Total 14,30,800

Hence, the appellants-claimants are entitled for a total enhanced compensation of Rs.14,30,800/-
along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a.
7.

In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER i.
Appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The judgment and award dated 21.03.2018 passed in MVC No.1482/2016 by X Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, MACT,
Bengaluru., is modified.
